claim_text: Each EF degree of damage has an expected, lower-bound and upper-bound wind speed set by expert elicitation (means of the experts' estimates); the expected value assumes normal conditions (no weak links, traditional construction, code compliance, maintenance) and the bounds cover deviations from them.
permitted_inference: Use EXP as the median gust of each degree and LB-UB as its spread.
prohibited_inference: Read the bounds as a stated percentile range or as measured scatter.
update_trigger: A revised EF scale (e.g. ASCE/SEI 49-21 implementation) changes the tables.

claim_text: EF wind speeds are three-second gusts estimated at the point of damage; the estimates vary with height and exposure.
permitted_inference: Take the EF speeds on the 3-second gust axis that Hazard delivers (10 m, open terrain), with a flagged bridge.
prohibited_inference: Claim the EF speeds are 10 m open-terrain values.
reasoning: The source states averaging time but not height or terrain; low-rise buildings sit near 10 m.
update_trigger: A source states the reference height and exposure.

claim_text: FR12 (one- and two-family residences, 1,000-5,000 ft2) has ten degrees of damage, expected gust 65 to 200 mph (table in EF_DEGREE_OF_DAMAGE_TABLE).
reasoning: Report text and SPC image identical.

claim_text: MBS (metal building systems; examples warehouses; large overhead doors; rigid frames, purlins, x-bracing) has eight degrees of damage, expected gust 67 to 155 mph.
permitted_inference: Use for RE_IND_WAREHOUSE (profile: one-storey steel, eight overhead doors).
prohibited_inference: Use WHB (tilt-up or heavy-timber warehouse) for a steel building.
reasoning: Report text and SPC image identical; the profile is a pre-engineered steel building.
update_trigger: Table revision; profile changes to tilt-up.

claim_text: LRB (low-rise building, 1-4 stories; examples office buildings; steel or concrete frame; BUR, single-ply or metal roof) has seven degrees of damage, expected gust 68 to 188 mph.
permitted_inference: Use for RE_COM_OFFICE_3S_SLAB (three storeys, steel, TPO roof).
reasoning: Report text and SPC image identical.

claim_text: FEMA assumes the damage states None, Slight, Moderate, Extensive and Complete correspond to mean building loss ratios of 0, 2, 10, 50 and 100%, identified from the damage descriptions with expert judgment, and interpolates linearly over 0-2, 2-5, 5-10, 10-50 and 50-100%.
permitted_inference: Use 2/10/50/100% as the cost of the Hazus damage state an EF degree matches, and 5% as the in-between point.
prohibited_inference: Call the costs calibrated or hurricane-specific evidence.
reasoning: The only published FEMA damage-state-to-cost correspondence for buildings; it is a general building statement used by the hurricane model.
update_trigger: A source gives repair cost per EF degree of damage.

claim_text: Hazus residential damage states: Slight = at most one window/door/garage door, roof cover loss over 2% to 15%; Moderate = roof cover over 15% to 50%, 1 to 3 deck panels; Extensive = roof cover over 50%, deck over 3 panels to 25%; Destruction = roof structure or wall frame failure.
reasoning: Component thresholds compare directly with the EF descriptions.

claim_text: Hazus metal-building damage states: Slight = one door or window; Moderate = slight roof or wall panel failures; Extensive = extensive window damage or roof sheathing loss, some frame damage likely; Destruction = significant roof and wall panel failures, significant frame damage.

Hazus engineered steel building damage states: Slight = one window or door, roof cover over 2% to 15%; Moderate = roof cover over 15% to 50%, windows over one to 2%, one or two deck panels; Extensive = roof cover over 50%, deck over two panels to 25%, local joist failures; Destruction = essentially complete roof failure or more than 25% of sheathing, wall envelope opened.

An EF degree of damage is a damage description, not a repair-cost ratio; the cost assigned to each degree in this cell is a judgment through the Hazus damage states (below-Slight = 1%, single-vs-multiple glazing = 5%, house shifted off its foundation = Extensive).
permitted_inference: Use the assigned costs as screening values with the sensitivity stated.
prohibited_inference: Present the costs as observed losses.
reasoning: No source prices EF degrees of damage; the judgment is bounded by the Hazus state descriptions.
update_trigger: A repair-cost study by EF degree; claims data by EF rating.

claim_text: Reading LB-UB as a 90% range (beta = ln(UB/LB)/3.29) gives beta 0.09 to 0.13; reading it as 68% or 95% changes the house damage at 120 mph from 36% to 41% or 34% (tornado).
permitted_inference: Use the 90% reading with the sensitivity stated.
prohibited_inference: Treat the spread as a measured fragility.
reasoning: The report gives no percentile; the effect is a few points.
update_trigger: A source states the bound percentile.

claim_text: Hazard delivers, for straight-line wind, an ASCE 7-22 3-second gust at 10 m, Exposure C (events at or above 58 mph, exponential excess, capped at 113 m/s = 252.8 mph) and, for a tornado, the EF band midpoint gust (75, 98, 123, 150.5, 183, 227 mph), with national median path length and width and a 150 km pooling radius.
permitted_inference: Accept a gust in mph from 0 to 255 for both pathways; accept the EF midpoint gust as a flagged bridge.
prohibited_inference: Accept an EF rating or category as input.
update_trigger: Hazard changes its fields or bounds.

claim_text: On Hazard's grid, the median cell sees 0.66 straight-line gust events a year at or above 58 mph, and the ASCE 700-year gust rebuilt from the layer is 99 / 107 / 113 mph (10th percentile / median / 90th percentile; maximum 167).
permitted_inference: Place the straight-line onset at 90% of the median design gust (96 mph).
prohibited_inference: Read the frequency below the ASCE 10-year gust as observed (it is extrapolated).

claim_text: Without an onset, straight-line yearly building loss is 370 to 500 times NRI (median cell); with the 96 mph onset it is 13 to 35 times; an onset at 90% of each cell's design gust gives about the same (13 to 36 times). Rank correlation with NRI is about 0.5.
permitted_inference: Adopt the onset; report the remaining gap and its Hazard-side causes.
reasoning: NRI undercounts and is a county average, so the check bounds the level, not the value.
update_trigger: Hazard revises the straight-line frequency; a building-level loss record.

claim_text: Tornado yearly building loss on Hazard's grid is 0.11 to 0.26 times NRI with rank correlation 0.91; the gap comes from Hazard's frequency and median path geometry, not the curve (a direct hit at the EF2 midpoint gust, 123 mph, already gives 18-44% damage and at EF3, 150.5 mph, 46-96%).
permitted_inference: Keep the tornado curve without an onset.
prohibited_inference: Raise the tornado curve to close a gap that sits in the hit geometry.

claim_text: The existing straight-line convective solar curve gives zero damage below R0 = 0.70 to 0.90 of the design pressure ratio, i.e. below 84% to 95% of the design gust.
permitted_inference: Support a no-damage onset for straight-line wind at about 90% of the design gust.

claim_text: The repository's failure-mode list names tornado or straight-line wind represented by a boolean or curve shift, and an unsupported pathway borrowing a neighbouring curve, as defects.
permitted_inference: Publish two governed pathways, each with its own evidence chain and records.

claim_text: The EF scale was built from tornado damage; the report does not address straight-line wind, and no source found establishes the EF degree-of-damage speeds for straight-line convective wind.
exact_locator: whole report (no straight-line or downburst mention)
permitted_inference: Label the straight-line records a T4 mechanism transfer of the EF evidence.
prohibited_inference: Claim the straight-line records are convective-specific evidence of the same tier as the tornado records.
reasoning: Wind loading on the envelope and frame depends on the gust in both cases; tornado-only effects (pressure drop, rotation, debris density) are inside the EF observations, so the transfer may overstate straight-line damage at a given gust.
update_trigger: A straight-line damage survey or loss study by building type.

claim_text: A documented repository precedent reuses a hurricane response for straight-line wind and tornado as a T4 cross-hazard proxy without duration conversion and with the EF midpoint gust as a T4 bridge.
permitted_inference: Name hurricane-curve reuse as the documented alternative; accept the EF midpoint gust as a flagged bridge.
